target_customer: Developers and operators building AI agent run businesses, plus buyers of agent run companies on its marketplace
problem: AI agents lack the identity, payments, communications and infrastructure needed to run a business end to end. Naive provides these primitives, company templates and managed agents.
business_model: Usage based API and platform for agents, company templates and a marketplace for agent run companies

founders.name: Sean Dorje
previous_startups: ezML (sold, per pulse2 coverage of the Series A)
founders.background_notes: Coverage says the founders have built together since age 14.

founders.name: Dennis Zax
previous_startups: ezML (sold, per pulse2 coverage of the Series A)

technical_complexity.rationale: Needs agent runtimes, identity and KYB, payments, phone and email provisioning, and company formation APIs, which combine infrastructure and regulatory integrations.

defensibility.rationale: Identity and primitives layer with regulated integrations (LLC formation, banking, insurance) is harder to copy than a wrapper, but the company says it builds on the open source Paperclip framework.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Autonomous company products from others (Polsia in late 2025, Replit's stated goal) emerged after founding; no acquisition found.

market_need_then: In 2025 interest in AI agents running work was high, but evidence of demand at founding is limited to the company's framing; later coverage shows investor interest.

branding.domain_note: Uses usenaive.ai; a different AI lab holds naive.ai per Brandfetch.

identity.voice_and_tone: Research lab voice with essays such as 'On Paperclip and open source'

branding.brand_signature: Ironic name 'Naïve' with diaeresis for a lab building autonomous companies
branding.community_and_virality: Series A coverage across several outlets and a viral X article on autonomous company infrastructure.

brand_strength.rationale: Distinctive ironic name and research lab voice with funding press, but a prefix domain and a similarly named lab at naive.ai add confusion.

outcome_analysis: Naive went through YC Spring 2025 and raised a $28.5M Series A in August 2026 led by Nexus Venture Partners. The raise rode the 2025 and 2026 interest in autonomous agents and a team of 12. Revenue and traction are not public, so success is early and based on funding signals.
notes: Series A confirmed by several outlets (pulse2, VCA Online, CXO Digital Pulse) and the YC page. Caplight lists a $2M seed dated 2025-11 and Tooljunction about $32M total; both unverified and not recorded as rounds. Founders' education and prior employers not found. Competitor searches returned only items dated after the batch, so the list is empty.
